subtopic: Moving to a new city on limited money
subtype: Approach: mental rehearsal of the daily commute before committing [Thinking]
passage: Ujjwal had two listings shortlisted in Bengaluru, one cheaper and further out. The thought of choosing on price alone felt wrong, so Ujjwal took a notebook and imagined a whole Tuesday in the cheaper place. Alarm at 6:10. Walk to the bus stop, wait. The crowded bus. Change at the junction. Office by nine, if the traffic was kind. Back at eight at night, the last stretch on an unlit road. Jeevan, an old college friend who lived nearby, said the buses thinned out after nine. On Sunday Ujjwal made the actual trip once, timing it. It took ten minutes longer than imagined, and the road really was dark. The cheaper flat no longer looked cheap.

qa.q: What time did the imagined alarm ring?
What did Ujjwal think about choosing on price alone?
qa.a: Ujjwal felt uneasy about it, and thought a full weekday should be pictured first to see the hidden costs.

qa.q: What could Ujjwal do next before deciding, and why?
qa.a: Ujjwal could try the evening trip once as well and count the cost of daily travel, because a hidden cost is only visible on the real route.

qa.q: How might Jeevan see Ujjwal's questions about the bus?
qa.a: Jeevan probably feels helpful as a local, and honest about the thinning buses, which is what Ujjwal needed to hear.

grounding: Before choosing a locality a person imagines a full weekday, including the commute and the return at night, and then tests the route once.

subtopic: Moving to a new city on limited money
subtype: Approach: mental rehearsal of the daily commute before committing [Thinking]
passage:
'Rent's ₹6,500, and it's got a balcony,' Suraj said, holding up the listing at the tea shop. 'I'm taking it.'
Thomas, who had lived in Bengaluru for three years, sipped his tea. 'Walk me through a Tuesday.'
'A Tuesday?'
'From the moment you wake up.'
'Okay. Office at nine. The flat's in Hoskote. So bus to the metro, metro to Whitefield, then walk. Maybe an hour?'
'Maybe?'
'Say I leave at seven-thirty. Coming back, leave office at seven, home by eight-thirty, if the bus comes.'
'And if it rains?'
Suraj was quiet. 'Then I don't know.'
'So find out. Go tomorrow at seven-thirty and actually do it.'
The next evening Suraj called. 'Two hours ten minutes. The bus only came every forty minutes. Coming back was worse.'
'Still want the balcony?'
'No,' Suraj said, laughing. 'I want to sleep. I'm looking near Whitefield, even if it's smaller.'

qa.q: What is the rent of the flat with the balcony?
What was Suraj feeling when Thomas asked 'And if it rains?'
qa.a: Uncertain and a little uneasy, realising he could not picture the trip once things went wrong.

qa.q: What else could Suraj rehearse before choosing a place near Whitefield?
qa.a: A late return and a rainy day, plus where groceries and weekday meals would come from.

qa.q: How does Thomas see Suraj's first plan?
qa.a: Thomas sees a listing chosen for a balcony, not for daily life, and uses questions so Suraj discovers the commute himself.

grounding: Shows a newcomer imagining a full weekday commute before choosing a flat and then testing the route once, exposing a hidden cost.

subtopic: Moving to a new city on limited money
subtype: Approach: mental rehearsal of the daily commute before committing [Thinking]
passage:
I'm Indu. When I moved to Mumbai for my first job, the cheapest room I found was with a retired teacher, Usha aunty, in Virar. ₹5,000 a month, home food, very kind. I nearly said yes on the phone.
Then I lay in bed and walked through a whole Monday in my head. Office in Lower Parel at 9:30. The Virar local, then a change. Wake at five-thirty, leave at six-forty. Coming home, the seven o'clock trains are the worst. Home at maybe 9:30. Eat, sleep, repeat. Where was the time for anything else?
Still, it was only imagination, so I tested it. The Monday before I joined, I did the journey at rush hour. I couldn't even get into the first train. It took two hours and ten minutes one way.
I called Usha aunty and thanked her. I took a shared room in Dadar for ₹9,000 instead. More money, but three extra hours every day.

qa.q: How much was the room with Usha aunty?
How did Indu feel after the test journey?
qa.a: Indu was probably drained and a bit shaken after not even getting into the first train, and clearer about the choice.

qa.q: What else could Indu weigh besides time?
qa.a: The extra ₹4,000 a month against the budget, and whether a middle option closer than Virar exists.

qa.q: How might Usha aunty feel about the call?
qa.a: Perhaps a little disappointed, but touched to be thanked and likely understanding about the long journey.

grounding: Shows a newcomer picturing a full weekday commute, then testing it at rush hour before choosing where to live.
